thread:
Priya: Quick check-in on dedicated capacity launch gating. Need final decisions on: reserved-pool quota slabs, short-term burst smoothing, eviction order, autoscale ramp rules, and billing grace windows. Trying to lock these for the customer pilot next month.

Sam: I'll run the quota-slab calc. Quick ask: do we keep 3 slab tiers (small/medium/large) or make it continuous? Customers like predictable buckets for billing.

Lina: From CS feedback, buckets are easier to sell. Recommend three tiers but allow soft custom top-ups. Example: small=2 nodes, medium=8, large=32. Also customers ask for 15% burst buffer on top of committed for emergencies.

Jordan: Ops constraints: preemption latency matters for opportunistic traffic. Eviction order should prefer opportunistic then best-effort sessions, not committed ones. Also recommend a minimum autoscale cooldown of 6 minutes and a ramp-up cap of +20% per minute to avoid sudden spin-ups.

Alex: Proposed autoscale policy for the pilot:
```yaml
autoscale_policy: pilot-v1
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 100
scale_up:
  trigger: sustained_cpu_above
  cpu_percent: 65
  lookback: 60s
  max_add_per_minute: 20%
scale_down:
  trigger: sustained_cpu_below
  cpu_percent: 35
  lookback: 300s
  grace_period: 6m
prewarm_behavior: predictive-with-warm-pool
warm_pool_size: 2
```
This lets us limit cost while smoothing spikes.

Maya: For billing, propose a 72-hour carryover window capped at 15% of monthly committed tokens. After 72h unused carryover expires. That keeps it simple for invoicing and predictable for customers.

Priya: Carryover 15%/72h seems reasonable. We should model worst-case monthly exposure and surface that in the contract. Sam, include that in the spreadsheet.

Sam: On it. I'll add a worst-case cost column. Also thinking of introducing a small opportunistic surcharge when customers hit burst beyond carryover (e.g., +10% on token rate) to align incentives.

Lina: Customers will accept a surcharge if it's clearly communicated and capped. Need sample invoice examples.

Jordan: Operational runbook items: 1) automated eviction script for opportunistic tasks, 2) region failover playbook, 3) a fast rollback path for rolling back autoscale config. I'll draft these and include commands.

Alex: I'll run a mixed workload test in staging for 72 hours with this autoscale policy and simulate sudden 3x traffic bursts to see tail latency.

Priya: Launch criteria (suggested):
- Stability: no P95 spikes >2x baseline during 72h staging run under mixed traffic.
- Cost: forecast variance <8% for pilot customers across synthetic bursts.
- Documentation: CS + legal reviewed contract language + billing examples.
- Observability: per-tenant telemetry for headroom, eviction events, and carryover usage.
- Rollout: canary to <5 customers with automated rollback.

Maya: Add compliance check for Private deployments (KMS logging on carryover transactions).

Sam: Question: do we want to expose an admin toggle for customers to opt into or out of carryover? That could complicate billing.

Lina: Offer it as an opt-in feature for pilot. Default off, but sales can enable in contract. That reduces billing churn.

Jordan: Also add a visible quota meter in Console so customers can see committed vs carryover vs opportunistic in realtime. That will reduce support load.

Priya: Good call. Action owners: Sam=quota slabs & cost model, Alex=autoscale tests & prewarm tuning, Jordan=runbook + console meter spec, Lina=billing copy & opt-in flow, Maya=compliance checks. Target: decision doc ready by Tuesday EOD.

devops-bot: Scheduled job queued: run-staging-mixedload -> pilot-v1-autoscale at 2024-04-20T02:00:00Z

Priya: Thanks all. We'll reconvene Tuesday to review test results and finalize launch gating. :white_check_mark:
